sources.reason: Original ORCA shell assembly modules with command, control-flow, I/O, line editor and memory-manager sources. Sampled control.asm contains named expression stack and flow-control logic. No independent build.
Original multi-application switcher with context preservation and GS/OS integration. Requires GNO/ME and ORCA/C plus ORCA/M according to author; compatibility not independently tested.

Z180 card firmware disassembly alongside 65C816/C host-side API/library, conversion helpers and protocol documentation. Do not conflate the card CPU with the host IIGS processor; semantic coverage varies across the generated listing.

Author's recovered 1981-1990 corpus includes utilities, BBS, games, languages and experimental filesystem/OS code. Kept at repository root rather than arbitrary subprojects. Author distinguishes successful assembly from wider runtime testing still to do.

Original 1987 graphics application source released by its authors for historical study. Assembly is stored in .TXT files. License is CC BY-NC-ND; availability does not imply unrestricted derivative-use permission.

Mark Reed editor sources covering commands, keyboard, display, disks, menus and printing. Main source identifies version 1.2 while README describes additions in 1.1; do not treat documentation version as current program version.

WIP annotated RGBDS source with named ball physics, brick and game-loop routines. README reports roughly 200 named functions and remaining unnamed data; no global completeness or byte-matching inference.
Explicitly unfinished HAM development-library decompilation. Author marks ham.c and fx.c complete but not the remaining library; sampled intro/multiboot source still contains behaviour questions.

Tutorial-oriented Python reconstruction with source-line references to the original Atari code. Inspected AI contains original velocity-table references but uses Python mechanisms; fidelity is attributed, not verified. Repository description mentions TypeScript, but inspected main tree establishes Python only.

Browser adaptation with source-derived rotation-matrix comments and separate landscape, model, player and game modules. No README or independent functional comparison; claims of exact source-derived elements are not whole-game equivalence.

Browser remake references original assembly geometry and terrain formulas, with substantive game-object, landscape and collision modules. Modern visual/gameplay adaptations remain distinct from a matching reconstruction.
Restored CP/M for the Quorum Spectrum clone, including BIOS, BDOS, CCP and bootloader. Author reports identical disk image and emulator boot; retained as upstream claims without independent build.
Retroworks original game source with artwork, music and build files. Requires older z88dk/Pasmo tooling; hardcoded addresses must be reconciled after changes and DSK generation includes manual steps.

6502 game and music port with headless Spectrum/jsbeeb comparison harnesses. README supersedes the repository's stale music-only description. Upstream notes slower sliding scroll and provisional colours; requires sideways RAM or Master. Claude credited explicitly.

6502 port with original-code comparisons, room streaming for stock Model B and sideways-RAM edition. Sampled collision code explains a colour-dependent blind spot. Upstream runtime/hardware claims not independently verified; repository explicitly describes AI-assisted development.
Main-68000 BIOS disassembly with constants, structures and decompression routines. README says sub-CPU and Z80 disassemblies are planned, so this is not complete coverage of all processors.
Small substantive IDA loader identifies Neo Geo ROM signature, sets 68000 CPU and maps memory/register regions. Uses historical IDA APIs; current-version compatibility not tested.

Standalone decoder targets reassemblable GNU AS/Sierra ASM68 output, presently focused on Mega Drive ROM hacking. Matching is the tool's goal; no independently verified universal round-trip guarantee.

Dave Dunfield CUBIX adapted for Nhyodyne, Duodyne and 6809PC with boot/drivers, applications and toolchain source. Keep whole repository and platform distinctions; no claim that every included application runs on every board.
Original evolving homebrew OS with ROM kernel/monitor, banked memory services and RAM command interpreter. README explicitly distinguishes implemented features from planned design.

Modern compiler rebuilding historical CP/M utilities to Z80 assembly and relocatable objects. Inspected compiler integrates frontend, AST/peephole passes and calling-convention checks. Output-size comparisons and full-language claims are upstream, not independently verified.

Multiuser MP/M II Z80 environment with custom banked XIOS and scripts selecting original binaries or building DRI PL/M sources. OS-wide emulator and reconstruction environment, not a game-specific emulation port. Default binary mode is not source reconstruction.

Monitor source recovered from deleted CP/M disk entries, with normalized readable copy and byte-preserved originals. Author documents presentation-only normalization, not synthesized repairs; the available HEX file is not assumed a proven build match.

Columbia Kermit archive customized for generic CP/M Plus and VT100, with M80/L80 build and tnylpo execution support. Distinct configured distribution, not a fresh independent protocol reconstruction; tool binaries not executed.
Source-driven SYSGEN rebuild with CBIOS, BDOS and ZCPR components for DJ2D at D000h. Author describes adaptations for other hosts; only specified Sorcerer configuration is classified here.

Partial function-by-function matching reconstruction with period Watcom tooling and separate decoded-assembly routines. README badge and prose show differing progress denominators; no headline exact percentage or whole-game matching claim promoted. Runtime badge reaches menu/world map, not proven full gameplay.

VS Code debug adapter and monitor client for Gearlynx, with cc65 symbol/source mapping, breakpoints and memory tooling. Extension source inspected; emulator/extension feature claims not independently exercised.
Repository description explicitly says beta binaries and issue tracking only, with source maintained privately. Do not classify it as available reconstructed source.

GitHub now contains a migration notice to https://codeberg.org/Kroc/elite-harmless. The destination could not be fetched in this pass; verify current source there before promotion instead of tracking an empty old mirror.
Description identifies an Unreal adaptation of a CPC project, but root lacks explanatory documentation. Further source/provenance review needed before classifying it as an RE-derived port.

Repository primarily experiments with running generated Sargon Z80 code through a portable Z80 emulator; inspect native CP/M output separately. Keep game-specific emulation out of promoted port listings.
